criteria.name: Client interview and fact development
criteria.description: Conducts a humane, effective client-intake interview with a guarded procurement director and develops the facts from the records and witnesses into a reliable, load-by-load chronology of what conformed, what did not, and what Empire did with each load.

subcriteria.name: Interview technique and rapport
subcriteria.description: Uses open-ended then focused questions, builds rapport, follows up on hints, and surfaces the client's guarded and undisclosed facts (the eight-day inspection gap, the resold Load D pallets, the supplier-switch motive) without pressure or flattery.

subcriteria.name: Records synthesis and chronology
subcriteria.description: Synthesizes the supply agreement, receiving and rejection records, consultant report, and production and carrier records into an accurate timeline and identifies the gaps and conflicts.

criteria.name: Conformity, rejection, and acceptance analysis
criteria.description: Correctly analyzes whether each load conformed, whether Empire rightfully and timely rejected, whether Empire accepted any goods (including by reselling part of Load D), and the seller's right to cure.

subcriteria.name: Warranties, conformity, and rejection elements
subcriteria.description: Identifies the governing sale-of-goods warranties and specifications and the elements of a rightful rejection of nonconforming goods, load by load.

subcriteria.name: Acceptance, cure, and timeliness applied to the facts
subcriteria.description: Applies acceptance (including acceptance by resale), the reasonable-time limit on rejection, and the seller's cure right to the disputed facts of the eight-day delay and the resold Load D pallets.

criteria.name: Seller's price claim and remedies strategy
criteria.description: Frames whether Ostervold can recover the full contract price or is limited to damages on each load, addresses the mixed causation of the short dating candidly, and builds a realistic exposure and defense theory.

criteria.name: Litigation posture and client counseling
criteria.description: Plans a response to the complaint and a discovery approach targeting the contested conformity, timeliness, and resale questions, and counsels the client candidly on options, exposure, and settlement.

criteria.name: Professional responsibility and written communication
criteria.description: Observes the Rule 4.2 no-contact limit with the represented opposing party and communicates clearly, in facts-and-advice form, without improper citation of law to the client.
